query: HRMP's $761 million community benefits include traffic/roadway work, MTA station improvements, 25+ acres of open space, a Community Impact Fund and social-services funding.

facts.text: The Board valued the Metropolitan Park community benefits package at $761 million.
The package includes traffic and roadway improvements.
The package includes improvements to the MTA transit station.
The package includes over 25 acres of new public open space.
The package includes a community impact fund.
The package includes funding for neighborhood social services.
The Board's chart itemizes $761 million upfront and another $150 million ongoing.
HRMP's executive summary advertises about $1 billion in community benefits.
HRMP's executive summary also uses $1.75 billion for investment into community needs.
HRMP's license requires milestones and budgets for community benefits proposed in its application.
The CAC submission schedules $150 million of fund payments during 2031–2060.
The operator reported distributing $2 million in grants in 2026.
News coverage reported that MTA had yet to agree to the proposed station overhaul.

conditions.text: HRMP delivered the promised roadway and traffic improvements.
HRMP delivered the promised MTA station improvements.
HRMP provided over 25 acres of new public open space.
HRMP funded the promised Community Impact Fund for the applicable periods.
HRMP supplied the promised neighborhood social-services funding.
Delivered benefits meet the promised package value using a defined and reconciled scope and term.

reference_verdict.reasoning: Sources disagree on the size of what was promised: the Board values it at $761M (over 20 years) while HRMP's filings and press say ~$1B or $1.75B, and the impact fund term is 20, 30 or to 2050/2060 depending on the source. The license binds the Application's benefits but sets no dollar figure. Delivery is mostly not yet due (opening 2030); the only delivery evidence (2026 impact-fund grants) is self-reported.

sources.title: GFLB Selection document (1 Dec 2025)
sources.specific_evidence: pdf p.18: "Community benefits valued at $761 million include significant traffic and roadway improvements, improvements to the ... (MTA)'s public transit station, over 25 acres of new public open space, a Community Impact Fund, and funding for neighborhood social services." Fn.7: "The community benefit commitment is confused by several factors."

sources.title: GFLB Report and Findings (Mar 2026)
sources.specific_evidence: p.29: "$761 million over the 20 years of their license term". p.30: "The Applicant committed to this $150 million over a 30-year license term." Chart 5: Park $299M, Transit $348M, Taste of Queens $60M, Neighborhood $41M, Impact Fund $13M = $761M upfront; +$150M ongoing = $911M.
sources.notes: 20- vs 30-year term inconsistency in the Board's own report.

sources.title: HRMP application Executive Summary (Jun 2025) and Supplement (Oct 2025)
sources.specific_evidence: Headline "$1 Billion in Community Benefits"; "a $1.75 billion dollar investment into community needs including infrastructure, parks and open space"; "$163 million impact fund and $50 million for local health, youth, and senior service initiatives will deliver approximately $1 billion in benefits."
sources.notes: $761M does not appear in HRMP's own filings.

sources.title: HRMP license award and Exhibit 1 License Conditions (19 Dec 2025; effective 15 Dec 2025)
sources.specific_evidence: Condition 3: "Hard Rock shall establish milestones and budgets concerning the community benefits proposed in the Application" and post public progress reports. Condition 10: monitor scope includes "Community benefits proposed in the Application".
sources.notes: No dollar figure in the license.

sources.title: Gaming Commission minutes, 3 Feb 2026 (adopted 16 Mar 2026)
sources.specific_evidence: Commissioners "required each licensee publicly post a listing of commitments promised to their representative community advisory committee, and, on a rolling basis, update the progress".
sources.notes: HRMP's list/progress reports not found on metropolitanpark.com or nycasinos.ny.gov.

sources.title: HRMP responses to CAC inquiries (29 Sep 2025)
sources.specific_evidence: Community Impact Fund schedule: Pre-award $3.2M; 2026-2030 $10M; 2031-2060 $150M; total $163.2M. Seven-member advisory board from 2026.

sources.title: Metropolitan Park Community Impact Fund page
sources.specific_evidence: "$2 million in grants distributed in 2026 alone"; ~$2M/yr 2026-2030; ~$5M/yr 2031-2050. "The Advisory Board does not approve grants."
sources.notes: Runs to 2050 here vs 2060 in CAC answers.

sources.title: Queens Daily Eagle, 'Construction prep underway for $8 billion Metropolitan Park casino' (25 Feb 2026)
sources.specific_evidence: "Cohen has also promised $1 billion in community benefits, including a complete overhaul of the 7 line train station at Mets-Willets Point, which the MTA has yet to agree to."
sources.notes: MTA agreement on station work outstanding as of Feb 2026.
